site.name: Luna-25 · Roscosmos (impact crater)
site.source: Luna-25 probable impact crater, LROC, lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1311, ME frame; Skyline site catalogue LUNA25_IMPACT, checked 2026-11-15.
site.reference: Where Luna-25 struck after its failed descent, about 58 S: shown for comparison, not as a landing site.

conventions.direct_sun: any part of the solar disk above the terrain skyline
conventions.daylight: any part of the solar disk above the flat horizon
conventions.earth_visible: Earth's centre above the terrain skyline plus a 0 deg margin (the default rule)
conventions.earth_center: Earth's centre above the terrain skyline
conventions.earth_any: any part of Earth's disc above the terrain skyline (reported as *_any)

dem.mode: windowed HTTP range requests (GDAL /vsicurl); no full download

provenance.dem_product: LOLA global DEM 118 m (USGS Astrogeology, Mar 2014)
provenance.frame: MOON_ME_DE421 body-fixed, 1737.4 km reference sphere, planetocentric site, LT+S aberration, no refraction

event_detection.completenessAssumption: At most one minimum and maximum per search interval. Multiple extrema and skyline discontinuities remain uncertified.

known_limits: Terrain used for the skyline at this site, by range (share of ray length): 0-200 km: Lunar_LRO_LOLA_Global_LDEM_118m_Mar2014 (118.451 m) 100%. Boulders and anything finer than the grid are not in the skyline.
Directions include reception light time and stellar aberration (LT+S). Atmospheric refraction is excluded.
Observer height is 2 m above the DEM surface.

Earth visibility is line of sight only: Earth's centre above the skyline plus a 0 deg margin (default), with the any-part-of-the-6371 km-disc rule alongside as *_any. It is not a radio link, and says nothing about link budget, antenna pointing or DSN availability.
The window is 365 days from 2026-11-14, not the 18.6-year lunar nodal cycle; the Sun's grazing angles and the Earth libration vary across that cycle.
The visible share of a disc treats the horizon as locally straight.
Detected events use extrema searches and Brent refinement to 1 s. Multiple extrema and skyline discontinuities can still hide events.

earth.rule: centre above the skyline (default); any part of the disc reported as *_any
